title: UxSID: Semantic-Aware User Interests Modeling for Ultra-Long Sequence
claim: Prior approaches either search per item at high cost or compress agnostically into static memory; ours shares memory across semantically grouped items.
layout: 3 panels side-by-side, top-to-bottom flow in each, red keywords in titles
description: Three parallel panels compare paradigms for modeling ultra-long user behavior sequences. Each panel has a red-keyword title: (a) search-based top-K selection (item-specific), (b) pre-trained item-agnostic compression, (c) UxSID semantic-specific compression. Each panel shows a tube of product icons (jacket, sandals, bananas, monitor, book) at the top. Below it are the method steps: (a) a magnifier does per-item online search and returns a top-K subsequence; (b) a gear icon does offline pre-training into a static 100-embedding colored grid; (c) candidate semantic IDs S1 Clothes, S2 Books and S3 Food feed offline pre-training into a semantic-specific memory, and a semantic query S1 retrieves from it. A dashed line separates offline from online parts. A candidate target feeds a trapezoid Ranking Model at the bottom of each panel.
caption: Comparison of different paradigms for ULSM. (a) Item-specific Search: Online filtering for each candidate, incurring high computational cost. (b) Item-agnostic Compression: Offline distillation into static memories, lacking target-specificity. (c) UxSID: A semantic-specific path that shares compressed interest memories among items with the same SIDs.
abstract: Modeling ultra-long user sequences involves a difficult trade-off between efficiency and effectiveness. While current paradigms rely on either item-specific search or item-agnostic compression, we propose UxSID, a framework exploring a third path: semantic-group shared interest memory. By utilizing Semantic IDs (SIDs) and a dual-level attention strategy, UxSID captures target-aware preferences without the heavy cost of item-specific models. This end-to-end architecture balances computational parsimony with semantic awareness, achieving state-of-the-art performance and a 0.337% revenue lift in large-scale advertising A/B test.
